name: Tourist Stay (entry stamp)

qualifying_event.description: The Dirección General de Migración y Extranjería (DGME) sorts countries of origin into two groups with different maximum authorised stays: Group 1 nationalities may stay up to 180 days, Group 2 nationalities up to 30 days (extendable to a 90-day maximum). A few nationalities have further bilateral exceptions (e.g. Russia at 90 days).
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Passport from a qualifying country; Group 2 nationalities need at least 90 days of passport validity remaining on entry.

value.note: Nationalities DGME classifies into 'Group 1', entitled to up to 180 days.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires holding a passport from a Group 1 country per DGME's classification.

value.note: Nationalities DGME classifies into 'Group 2', entitled to up to 30 days, extendable to a 90-day maximum, and requiring 90+ days of passport validity on entry.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires holding a passport from a Group 2 country per DGME's classification; passport must have at least 90 days' validity remaining.

outcome.duration_length: up to 180 days (Group 1) or up to 30 days, extendable to a 90-day maximum (Group 2), per entry

sources.title: La Nación (Costa Rican newspaper) -- '180 or 30 days? How Costa Rica grants maximum stay to foreign tourists by nationality', describing DGME's own group classification

notes: NEW COUNTRY, first Costa Rica route. IMPORTANT, COMMONLY MISSTATED FACT: Costa Rica does NOT give a flat 90-day tourist stay to everyone -- DGME sorts nationalities into two groups with genuinely different maximums (up to 180 days vs. up to 30, extendable to 90). STATUS SET TO DRAFT: migracion.go.cr's own pages (the natural tier-1 source for this classification) returned HTTP 403 to automated fetching throughout this pass; sourced instead from a single tier-4 newspaper article describing the government's own classification, without independently reaching the classification criteria or the specific country-to-group mapping. No financial-means or return-ticket requirement was confirmed in the source, though these are commonly required in practice per other (unconfirmed) sources -- not invented here.
